service.name: Wedding cocktail hour music
service.serviceType: Live music for wedding cocktail hours
service.description: Jazz duo, acoustic duo and solo guitarist bookings for wedding cocktail hours across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor.

faqs.q: Do you need music during cocktail hour?
faqs.a: You need something, and live musicians are the option guests notice. Silence in that hour feels like a gap in the day, because the couple is away for photographs and nothing else is happening yet. A duo covers the hour without asking anyone for their attention. Signet Artists books cocktail hour musicians across Denver and the Colorado mountains.

faqs.q: How many songs for cocktail hour?
faqs.a: Roughly fifteen to twenty for a 60-minute hour and closer to thirty for 90 minutes, because a standard runs three to four minutes. Live musicians don't work to a count: the set runs continuously and tunes stretch or shorten to the crowd.

faqs.q: Will anyone actually notice the music?
faqs.a: Not consciously, and that's the hour going right. Guests notice that the evening felt hosted more than they notice which tunes played.
Yes, that's what the level is set for. Two guests who have just met can talk across it without raising their voices, and the duo adjusts on the spot if a terrace fills up or empties out.

faqs.q: Instrumental or vocals for cocktail hour?
faqs.a: Instrumental, for most of the hour. A voice pulls attention to the words, and guests who are mid-introduction feel that as competition. Where a wedding wants a voice anyway, a singer can lead the hour and the level comes down to match.

faqs.q: Is a duo enough for 60 to 70 guests?
faqs.a: Yes. Two musicians are the right size for that count, from twenty at one table to eighty across ten. On a big terrace or a lawn spread wide, the trio reaches the far edge at the same level the near edge hears.

faqs.q: What does an outdoor cocktail hour need?
faqs.a: A covered, level and dry spot for the musicians, power run to it, and a move-indoors call written before the day. Colorado evenings get cold fast after sunset, and instruments and electronics both stop behaving in the cold.

faqs.q: How far ahead should we book, and what paperwork comes with it?
faqs.a: Wedding dates book ten to twelve months out, and twelve to eighteen for a mountain venue or a fall Saturday, so the cocktail hour is usually decided when the band is. A certificate of insurance, a W-9 and an itemized invoice come in the same email as the contract, with a personal contact for the day.
